sections.changelog:
Added

  • Plugin skeleton: header (Requires at least 7.0, Requires PHP 8.1, Requires Plugins woocommerce, Update URI), version and path constants, PSR-4 autoloader mapping `MVweb\Telegram\Hub` to `src/`
  • `Plugin` orchestrator booting the queue worker, the log cleanup and the module registry on `plugins_loaded`
  • Module registry with per-module toggles: a module declares its own requirements and is skipped when they are not met
  • WooCommerce orders module hooked on `woocommerce_checkout_order_processed` and `woocommerce_store_api_checkout_order_processed`, so both the classic and the block checkout are covered
  • Duplicate protection through the `_mvweb_tg_sent` order meta flag, written before dispatch and read through the order CRUD API
  • HPOS compatibility declared via `FeaturesUtil::declare_compatibility( 'custom_order_tables' )`; every order read goes through `wc_get_order()` and the CRUD getters
  • Background delivery through Action Scheduler (group `mvweb-tg`), one job per recipient, with a WP-Cron fallback if Action Scheduler is unavailable
  • Retry policy: 1, 5 and 15 minutes on network errors, HTTP 5xx and 429 (honouring `retry_after`); 400 and 403 are never retried
  • Telegram Bot API client with a normalised response shape, a 15-second timeout and a configurable API host for sites that cannot reach api.telegram.org
  • Message formatter: escaping for Telegram HTML, `wp_kses` whitelist for the editable template, label-only line collapsing, and tag-aware truncation that closes open tags instead of letting the API reject the message
  • Editable order template with 16 macros and a configurable line-item limit
  • Delivery log in a dedicated `mvweb_tg_log` table recording failures and retries only, with per-order filtering, pagination and a daily cleanup event
  • Settings screen under the MVweb Hub on Admin UI Kit v2 with four tabs — Bot, WooCommerce orders, Log, Help — saved through the native Settings API
  • Diagnostics: "Check recipients" (getChat per chat) and "Send a test message", both reporting per recipient; token verification through `getMe` on save
  • Bot token can be defined as `MVWEB_TG_BOT_TOKEN` in wp-config.php, which overrides the stored value; the stored token is never rendered into admin HTML
  • Non-destructive `uninstall.php`: data is removed only when "Delete data on uninstall" was switched on, and order meta is swept in batches from both postmeta and the HPOS meta table
  • Internationalization: `load_plugin_textdomain`, `.pot` and a complete `ru_RU` translation
  • Plain-language advice for a failed delivery: the Telegram error is translated into the next step to take ("the recipient blocked the bot — ask them to press Restart"), shown both in the log and in the diagnostics report, with the raw API answer kept underneath
  • Macros insert themselves into the template on click, at the cursor position
  • Help tab explains where a chat ID comes from for a person, a group and a channel, and what each one looks like
  • Question-mark tips on the token, the API address, the recipients, the template, the item limit, the uninstall switch and the attempt counter
  • Setup card on the first tab: the four steps of connecting the plugin with a progress bar, each one marked done or waiting, so a partial setup shows what is still missing instead of looking finished
  • Line items are laid out over two lines — name, then the figures indented underneath — because shop product names are long, wrap in Telegram, and a "× 2 · 10 400 ₽" tail glued to a wrapped name is unreadable
  • A line item with more than one piece now spells out the arithmetic: "2 × 5 200 ₽ = 10 400 ₽", with the sum in bold. The old single figure was the line total but read as the price of one piece
  • Redesigned default message: emoji markers per line, the order date in italics, payment and shipping alongside the total, and the wp-admin link as an "Open the order →" anchor instead of a naked address. Empty macros still drop their whole line, so a short order stays short
  • The macro glossary is a `dl` on a single grid: codes line up in one column, each description sits on the same line as its own macro and can only grow inside its own cell. The earlier multi-column list let a wrapped description drift into the neighbouring track, which is why it had been stacked under the code
  • The "insert the standard template" action follows the studio pattern for a helper control under a field — `.mvweb-btn--sm` as a direct child of `.mvweb-form-row__field`, explanation in `.mvweb-form-row__desc` — instead of a hand-rolled paragraph with a ghost button
  • "Insert the standard template" button next to the template field, so the ready-made layout can be brought back after edits — or picked up on a site that already stored an older default
  • The test message now previews the real template on the most recent order rather than a stub line, answering "how will it look" before a customer places an order. Falls back to the plain line on a shop with no orders
  • "Find my chats" next to the recipients field: asks the Bot API which chats the bot has taken part in and lists their ids. A private channel has no @name and shows its id nowhere in Telegram, so this was the missing step — being promoted to administrator is itself an event the bot receives, so the channel appears without anyone writing in it. Explains itself when the list is empty, including the case of a webhook taking the updates
  • Instructions sit next to the field they explain instead of pointing at the Help tab: how to get a token (four steps, folded once the bot works) under the token field, and where a chat ID comes from for a person, a group and a channel under the recipients field — naming the actual connected bot, so the steps can be handed to a colleague as they are. The Help tab stays as the longer read

Fixed

  • Every request logged "Translation loading for the mvweb-telegram-hub domain was triggered too early". Reading any setting merges the defaults, and the default message template is a translatable string, so the first `Settings::get()` pulled the textdomain in on `plugins_loaded` — a just-in-time load, which WordPress 6.7 reports as `_doing_it_wrong`. The plugin now boots on `init`; nothing it hooks fires earlier than that
  • An order with no payment method left a stray separator in the message: the total and the payment method shared a line, so the line was not empty and survived the empty-line rule while the "·" between them had nothing left to separate. The default template keeps one macro per line
  • The narrow modifier on the two numeric fields never applied: the UI Kit caps an input at 480px through `input.mvweb-input`, which outranks a bare class selector, so a field for a number between 1 and 50 was as wide as the twelve-row template textarea
  • A table wider than its card was cut off with no way to reach the rest — the Kit wrapper clips its overflow to keep the rounded corners. On a phone that removed exactly the column of example chat numbers the help table exists for. The three tables now scroll sideways instead
  • "Delete token" — the only irreversible action in the plugin — was the quietest button on the screen: ghost styling identical to "Show all", no confirmation, and sitting outside the card grid, while the fully reversible "Insert the standard template" did ask for confirmation. It is now a danger button inside its own card that says what will be lost, and both it and "Clear the log" ask first
  • The empty log claimed "every notification went through" even when a filter was active and the log was not empty at all. The filter state was already computed one line above and simply not used
  • Two brand-filled buttons faced each other on the orders tab: the sticky save bar is on screen at all times, so the diagnostics "Send a test message" was competing with it for the same role
  • The environment warning was printed twice on the plugin's own screen — once as an admin notice carrying the plugin-name prefix, once as the card inside the tab that explains it properly. The notice is now left to the plugins list, where the prefix is what identifies it
  • The default template lost its "Items:" heading in every message. Collapsing label-only lines ran over the rendered text, where a static heading is indistinguishable from a label whose macro came out empty; the decision now happens during substitution, where it is known which macros a line carried
  • Deactivating the plugin left queued deliveries in place, so they fired on the next activation. Action Scheduler is now asked by group with an empty hook — passing hook and group together sends it down the single-action path, which matches only jobs with empty arguments — and WP-Cron is cleared with `wp_unschedule_hook()` instead of a `wp_next_scheduled()` loop that cannot see events carrying a payload
  • Truncating a long message could cut through an escaped entity and leave a bare `&`, which Telegram rejects with a 400, losing the whole notification; the fragment is now dropped, and the order link is appended to the ellipsis so it survives the cut
  • Verifying a token saved together with a custom API address checked it against the previous host, reporting a false failure exactly when a proxy was being set up
  • A successful save showed no confirmation: core files its notice under the `general` slug, which the screen was filtering out
  • Descriptions coming back from the Bot API were printed into admin notices unescaped
  • The message template was unslashed twice, eating the operator's backslashes
  • `Table::maybe_install()` was never called, so a schema version bump would not have migrated anything on plugin update
  • Help tab rendered one word per line: `.mvweb-steps li` is a two-column grid, so the paragraph next to `` became a third grid item and dropped into the 32px counter column. Step content is wrapped in a single element, as the UI Kit reference does, and FAQ answers use `.mvweb-faq__body` so the answer fuses to its question
  • The sticky save bar floated over the last card — white on white — hiding the text under it, because these tabs are barely taller than one screen; it is anchored to the end of the form instead
  • The save bar stopped floating halfway down the page and wedged itself against the next card. Sticky only floats within its own parent, and each tab posts its own form with the diagnostics card sitting after it — so the bar ran out of parent at the closing tag. The bar now ends the tab panel and reaches its form through the button's `form` attribute, which also keeps the action buttons out of a nested form
  • The save button was rendered by `submit_button()`, which adds WordPress' own `button` class; `.wp-core-ui .button` outranks `.mvweb-btn--primary`, so the button came out in the default blue outline instead of the brand fill. Written out as the boilerplate does it
  • Macro descriptions wrapped under the neighbouring column and stopped belonging to any macro in particular; each macro now sits above its own description
  • Saving the Bot tab reported "these recipients were skipped: Array". WordPress runs the sanitiser a second time inside `update_option()`, by then over the parsed list; casting that array to a string produced the literal `Array`, which then failed validation and reported itself as a rejected recipient
  • The token field was `type="password"`, so browsers treated the form as a login: offering keychain entries on focus and asking to save a password on every save. It is an API key and is always rendered empty, so it is a text field with autofill hints switched off

Changed

  • Calls to the Bot API go through `wp_safe_remote_post()`. The API host is operator-editable and the token travels inside the URL, so the address is now validated by core against loopback and private ranges; a genuinely internal proxy stays reachable through `WP_ACCESSIBLE_HOSTS`
  • The schema check no longer runs on storefront requests. It reads a non-autoloaded option, which is one query per page view for a migration that can only matter in the admin, in cron or under WP-CLI
  • One word for one thing: a chat is addressed by its "number" everywhere, with "chat ID" named once in the help as what the rest of the internet calls it. The macro list lost "Internal", "Billing" and "wp-admin" along the way
  • Instructions under the recipients field fold away once there is a recipient, exactly like the token steps do — three cases of prose stood four times taller than the field they explain and never folded. "Find my chats" stays outside the fold, since that is the step which remains useful afterwards
  • The active tab is marked with `aria-current`, the delivery report uses the Kit's alert title, and the empty log has the icon and title the Kit component provides — the state was a bare paragraph in a 48px-tall box
  • Instruction blocks are set in the small size rather than the extra-small one: they carry the longest connected text on the screen, and the macro list next to them was already a size larger
  • The completed-step marker takes the Kit's success tokens instead of a hand-picked green, and the toolbar keeps the Kit's own spacing
  • The delivery log can be filtered by error code as well as by order
  • The WooCommerce orders tab states plainly when WooCommerce is missing or the module is switched off, instead of looking ready to work
  • Log timestamps are shown in the site timezone instead of UTC
  • The "nothing is sent yet" warning names what is actually missing instead of listing every requirement — asking for a bot token a minute after it was saved reads as an accusation
  • The macro reference is folded away: sixteen macros with descriptions pushed the item limit and the diagnostics buttons off the screen
  • Bundled `class-mvweb-menu.php` refreshed from `shared/` — its hub catalogue still listed two other plugins at older versions
  • Interface copy rewritten for shop owners rather than developers: no `chat_id`, no talk of hooks and payloads
